newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Macronix up on T$200 bln wafer plan.
newsitem.headline: Macronix up on T$200 bln wafer plan.

text.p: Taiwan microchip maker Macronix International Co surged at mid-morning on Friday after saying on Thursday it would invest more than T$200 billion within 10 years to build advanced 12-inch wafer fabrication plants.
With 70 minutes left, at 0250 GMT, Macronix was up the daily seven percent limit to T$74. It was the most heavily traded share on Friday with volume at 77.3 million shares.
"Macronix's announcing the expansion is no surprise at all because other local competitors have already done so," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
"However, we can still see the confident outlook of local semiconductor makers in their daring to launch so many huge projects," Hung said.
Macronix became the sixth Taiwan microchip maker to announce a multibillion-dollar high-tech expansion.
"The electronic industry is Taiwan's king industry now. And the semiconductor industry is the king of kings," Hung added.
While huge at T$200 billion, the Macronix plan is dwarfed by 10-year development plans unveiled in recent months by market leader Taiwan Semiconductor and No.2 maker United Microelectronics.

Taiwan Semicon pledged in April to spend T$400 billion on six advanced production lines in the new Tainan park, the biggest investment in Taiwan to date. United Micro went its rival one better in June, announcing a T$500 billion project to build 12-inch wafer fabs in the same Tainan high-tech park.
Macronix said it soon would announce at least two major cooperation projects with foreign clients that would yield significant -- and badly needed -- new orders.
Analyst Hung forecast Macronix was on track to report earnings per share of T$1.02 in 1997 and T$1.35 in 1998.
